answerChoices.text: one real root and one imaginary root

solutions.text:
For a real solution, \(x\ge3.\) Then \(x+4>x-3,\) so \[ \sqrt{x+4}>\sqrt{x-3}. \] Consequently \(\sqrt{x+4}-\sqrt{x-3}+1>1,\) and it cannot equal zero. The original equation is a real radical expression, so nonreal roots are outside its domain.

The correct answer is A.
hints: For real square roots the domain requires \(x\ge3\)
On that domain, compare \(\sqrt{x+4}\) directly with \(\sqrt{x-3}\)
